questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go outside of Europe, I wanted to visit Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was slow to send out information, but when they did, they were good at providing a lot of information. Keep an eye on your Western email. I was going in the fall semester and they didn't really start sending out information until the summer break.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The first week was an orientation week for international students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was possible to apply for different housing options. I lived in Alumni house which I would recommend as you have your own bedroom and share a kitchen, living room and bathroom with three other people. In some of the other housing facilities, you share a bedroom with one roommate.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: It was possible to have a meal plan, but i opted out of that as i had a kitchen in the residence where i lived.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It takes a long time before you receive any housing information, I arrived in Canada at the end of August and I received the information about applying for housing at the end of June. I would recommend to live on campus as it makes it easier to interact with other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The kitchen in the apartment is empty and you have to buy everything when you arrive. I would recommend buying these things with your roommates and going to Value Village or Dollarama which are two cheap stores. There is also no bedding in the bedroom and you will have to buy this before arriving.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You applied through a website where it was possible to see all courses. It was very difficult to figure out which courses you could take, as many courses were part of a specific program.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international team at the university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very successful. I had a hard time finding classes, and most of my classes ended up not being very relevant to what I was interested in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply to a lot of classes in the beginning of the process as it is difficult to get a spot in the classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had level 2000 courses, which are second-year courses. The level of difficulty varied greatly depending on the course

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching was similar to how classes are in Danish Gymnasium. In all my classes it was a must that the students participated in the class discussions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Not 'lost in translation'
Foundations of global communications
Media and social movements
Ethics in digital media

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you want an easy course I can recommend Not 'lost in translation', the professor was very kind.

Foundations of global communications was a very interesting course, but difficult. There is a lot of reading, and the professor expects a lot from his students. But he is very talented and you will learn a lot from taking this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to buy all the basics for your apartment if you live on campus. I spent the first 5000kr just on these things. It's everything from plates to a duvet and hangers. Hold off on buying the basics for the kitchen, sometimes you can get what other exchange students have left behind.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was a lot more expensive than i expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of different social activities and clubs available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use some of all the gym facilities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend renting a car and driving to the US, or around in Ontario. I enjoyed visiting Algonquin national park, Banff and New York.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Canadians are nice, but it can be difficult to get to know them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are kind

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Don't stress too much - You will receive all the information needed about housing and classes in time for your arrival. 
2. Go explore - London is not the most exciting city, therefore I would recommend seeing other places while you are there.
3. Time passes by quickly, enjoy that you are on exchange and are getting that experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive in the international orientation week, this is a great way to meet other international students and make new friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot about myself by being on exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning the Canadian school system. There are quizzes, assignments that count towards your final grade, the professor takes attendance and you need to participate in the debates in class as this also counts towards your final grade.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
